items.title: SENATE BUDGET SHOWDOWN GOES TO THE WIRE

left.headline: CUTS WOULD HIT FAMILIES FIRST
left.summary: Placeholder summary. Progressive outlets emphasize which programs face the deepest reductions and who depends on them. They frame the impasse as a choice about priorities, not arithmetic.

neutral.headline: NEGOTIATORS RUN OUT OF CALENDAR
neutral.summary: Placeholder summary. Wire services report both caucuses remain roughly $80 billion apart with three legislative days left. A short-term continuing resolution is the most likely outcome.

right.headline: SPENDING SPREE MUST END
right.summary: Placeholder summary. Conservative outlets frame the standoff as a long-overdue fight against runaway federal spending. They argue the deficit, not the shutdown threat, is the real emergency.

items.title: BORDER BILL COLLAPSES AGAIN ON THE HOUSE FLOOR

left.headline: ASYLUM PROTECTIONS AT STAKE
left.summary: Placeholder summary. Left-leaning outlets highlight the asylum restrictions in the draft text and the objections from advocacy groups. They frame the failure as avoiding a harmful compromise.

neutral.headline: VOTE COUNT NEVER MATERIALIZED
neutral.summary: Placeholder summary. Neutral reporting notes leadership pulled the bill after failing to secure 218 votes. Both parties blame the other for the collapse.

right.headline: ENFORCEMENT GUTTED, AGAIN
right.summary: Placeholder summary. Right-leaning coverage focuses on enforcement provisions stripped in committee. The bill is described as a messaging exercise rather than a border fix.

items.title: STREAMING GIANT PULLS DOCUMENTARY AFTER BACKLASH

left.headline: SUBJECTS SAY THEY WERE MISLED
left.summary: Placeholder summary. Left-leaning coverage centers on participants who say their interviews were edited misleadingly. Editorial standards, not censorship, drive the framing.

neutral.headline: PLATFORM CITES LICENSING
neutral.summary: Placeholder summary. Trade press reports the title was removed at the end of a licensing window, days after a public complaint. The timing remains unexplained.

right.headline: ANOTHER QUIET CANCELLATION
right.summary: Placeholder summary. Conservative commentary treats the removal as evidence of a narrowing window for dissenting films. The platform's explanation is described as vague.

items.title: IS ANYONE STILL READING PAST THE HEADLINE?

left.headline: OUTRAGE PAYS BETTER THAN CONTEXT
left.summary: Placeholder summary. A progressive essayist blames ad-driven incentives that reward inflammatory headlines. The fix proposed is funding models that pay for depth.

neutral.headline: ATTENTION IS THE SCARCE RESOURCE
neutral.summary: Placeholder summary. A media researcher summarizes studies showing most shares happen without a click. The problem is described as structural rather than partisan.

right.headline: THE PRESS EARNED THE DISTRUST
right.summary: Placeholder summary. A conservative columnist argues that headline-only reading is a rational response to years of corrected stories. Trust, the piece says, is a lagging indicator.
